title: Three ways to take control
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Do you know how someone could take control of a company?
Jose asked: does anybody know what a hostile takeover is? A student said: you are coming in and taking controlling interest in the company against the current executives and management.

It is a very aggressive thing, Jose said. He gave examples of well-known takeovers of food and chocolate companies. There is a variety of methods to gain control of a company, and he explained three categories.
The first is a tender offer: the acquirer makes a public offer to buy the target company's stock at a fixed price that is higher than the market price.

The second is a proxy fight, he said: the acquirer tries to convince enough shareholders to appoint them as proxies, who can then use their voting power to accept a takeover. This is a very interesting one.

Jose said he was involved in one of these with a company, where the major shareholders were not happy with management. They went to other shareholders and rallied, and took over and fired the management.

The third was a creeping tender offer, he said: slowly buying the shares. The chief executive was very cautious, because he probably felt: this is pretty dangerous, when he started getting to know who the buyer was.
In the book, he said, the buyer offers a price above the market, gets the banks together to put the deal together, and wants to take the company private.
What is the weakest point in the control of a company you know?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write who controls the company you know best.
Write what shareholders could do if unhappy.
Write the three methods in your own words.
Write one reason someone would want to buy a company they run.
Write who you would ask to explain it properly.

check.q: What did a student say a hostile takeover is?
choices: Taking controlling interest against current management

check.q: What is a tender offer, as Jose explained it?
choices: A public offer to buy stock at a fixed price above the market price

check.q: What is a proxy fight, as Jose explained it?
choices: Convincing shareholders to appoint you as proxy to use their voting power

recap: Know the three ways control of a company can change. It is education, not financial or legal advice.
